Team — forwarding Orchid’s ask and the attached usage file. TL;DR: customer wants to double tokens for next 3–4 months; preference to co-term with Oct renewal if we can make numbers attractive. My suggested options to put in front of them:

1) Burst add-on: month-to-month; no discount; immediate invoice; simplest operationally.
2) 6-month committed top-up: commit to the uplift for 6 months, 8% discount on incremental units, invoiced monthly but contract amendment for term.
3) Annualized & co-term: customer pays/commits now for uplift annualized to Oct renewal; 12% discount on incremental units, amendment and pro-rata invoice to align to renewal.

Questions:
- Ben: can you confirm margin/support for 12% (annualized) vs 8% (6mo)? If you need a not-to-exceed cap for discount authority let me know.
- Kimberly: co-term legal process — are there standard clauses we should include (pro-rata, no SLA change, payment terms)?
- Tessa: billing mechanics — if we pro-rate to Oct, do you need a separate invoice now or can we roll into the renewal invoice?

Attachments: Orchid_TopUp_Usage_Spreadsheet.xlsx

Thanks — want to get back to them with a crisp pricing table and a one-page amendment draft by EOD.

-Neha

Fine to proceed with the three-option approach. Confirming pricing guardrails:
- Monthly burst: list pricing (no discount).
- 6-month committed top-up: up to 8% discount on incremental usage (approved).
- Annualized (co-term) option: approve up to 12% discount on incremental uplift if customer signs amendment to commit uplift amount and agrees to standard payment terms.

If the uplift is very large (> $120k ARR incremental), I’d want to review the final ask with sales leadership before exceeding 12%. For the customer-facing table, provide both absolute and % savings.

Thanks for the ping. Quick legal notes on co-terming and top-ups:
- Co-terming is straightforward — we would add a one-page amendment that: describes the uplift units, effective date, pro-rata invoicing to align to Oct renewal, and preserves existing SLA/credits.
- Payment terms: prefer to invoice the pro-rated portion now (so revenue recognition aligns) but we can also invoice at renewal if finance agrees; if they want to delay payment, we need explicit PO/workflow.
- Security/compliance scope: no change if they are not adding new integrations.

I’ve attached a short amendment draft (Proposed_Amendment_Draft_v1.pdf) with comments where we usually add finance/legal language. If they want co-term we can send the amendment via DocuSign; I added placeholders for the uplift amounts.

-Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts

Hi Hannah / Chris — thanks for the patience. Based on the forecast you shared we ran the numbers and have three options for you to consider. I summarized key commercial and operational notes below and attached the amendment draft.

Orchid top-up options (incremental units = forecast delta from attached spreadsheet):

Option A — Monthly burst (fastest)- Description: month-to-month add-on for incremental usage; charged at list incremental unit price- Discount: 0%- Billing: immediate monthly invoices- Pros/Cons: simplest operationally; no contract amendment required

Option B — 6-month committed top-up- Description: commit to uplift for 6 months; amendment documents commitment- Discount: 8% on incremental units- Billing: invoiced monthly under amendment- Pros/Cons: modest savings; no co-term work required beyond amendment

Option C — Annualized & co-term (recommended if you prefer price certainty)- Description: commit and annualize uplift now; we add a one-page amendment and align to your Oct renewal (pro-rated invoicing today for term through Oct)- Discount: 12% on incremental units- Billing: pro-rata invoice now + balance at renewal; amendment via DocuSign- Pros/Cons: best unit economics and contract simplicity at renewal; requires amendment and PO/approval now

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 20-min call to confirm which option you prefer and uplift quantity (I’m available tomorrow 10–11am PT or 2–4pm PT).
2) If Option C, we’ll send the amendment via DocuSign (link: https://www.docusign.com/tx/ORCH-4582-amendment) and provide a line-item invoice for the pro-rated portion.
3) If Option B or A, I’ll send the appropriate SOW/amendment or order form.

Attachments: Proposed_Amendment_Draft_v1.pdf, Orchid_TopUp_Usage_Spreadsheet.xlsx

Thanks — trying to keep this as frictionless as possible. If you want, we can also include a short one-page summary for procurement.
